items.item_text: California Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)
Graduation from an accredited school of social work with a master's degree in social work (MSW)
Must be able to master detailed and complex information regarding benefits and coordination of care
A minimum of three (3) years' recent experience in the field of social work
Experience providing short-term, evidence-based psychotherapy
Extensive, broad-based clinical experience
Experience working in a healthcare setting
Experience in identifying and analyzing care/service needs for patients
Training and experience in evidence-based therapies (CBT, Behavioral Activation, Problem-Solving Therapy, and similar)

The Collaborative Care Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) provides integrated behavioral health services to adults ages 50 and older within UC Davis Health’s Primary Care clinics. Working alongside psychiatrists, Primary Care providers, and multidisciplinary healthcare teams, the LCSW supports patients experiencing mild to moderate behavioral health concerns, including depression, anxiety, grief, and adjustment-related challenges.
15% - Communication/Collaboration/Teamwork

Using advanced clinical judgment and evidence-based practices, the LCSW provides short-term individual psychotherapy, psychosocial assessments, individualized treatment planning, care coordination, and referrals to community resources. The position addresses patients’ biopsychosocial needs while promoting access to care, patient self-determination, confidentiality, and active participation in healthcare decisions.
5% - Professional Development

As an integral member of the collaborative care team, the LCSW contributes to high-quality, patient-centered services through interdisciplinary consultation, effective communication, and continuous improvement initiatives. The position practices in accordance with the NASW Code of Ethics, UC Davis Health policies, and applicable state and federal regulations.
Demonstrated ability to work on a multidisciplinary team
Must have solid psychosocial assessment skills
Must demonstrate ability to effectively and efficiently handle a demanding workload involving multiple tasks
Excellent analytical, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills
Skills to perform in-depth chart analysis to provide accurate information in a concise, informative manner
Requires a high level of clinical judgment, problem-solving skills, creativity, organizational and priority-setting abilities, with excellent communication skills
Knowledge of care/services provided in differing levels of care in ambulatory and institutional settings
Knowledge of community resources
Knowledge of biopsychosocial and behavioral health treatment plans
Ability to work with all levels of staff, both inter- and intra-departmental, to create a cooperative relationship and positive working environment
Knowledge of legal requirements and guidelines for providing psychiatric services, including mental status exams, suicide risk assessments, 5150 applications, and mandated reporting requirements
